questions.stem: The ferry at Double Bay is being pulled into the wharf by a rope at a speed of 25m/min. The rope is attached to a point on the ferry 6m vertically below the level of the wharf. At what rate is the rope being drawn in, when the ferry is 28m from the wharf?
questions.hint: Right triangle r² = x² + 6²; dr/dt = (dr/dx)(dx/dt) with dx/dt = 25.

steps.explain: Let \(x\) be the horizontal distance to the wharf and \(r\) the rope length. They form a right triangle with the 6 m vertical side.

questions.stem: Two straight roads, Lagoon Road and Mitchell Street, intersect at an angle of \(120^\circ\). Audrey leaves the intersection at 9:00 am and travels on Lagoon Road at a constant speed of 50 kilometres per hour. Braxton leaves the intersection at 10:00 am, travelling along Mitchell Street at a constant speed of 60 kilometres per hour. Taking \(t=0\) at the time of Braxton's departure from the intersection: show that the distance between Audrey and Braxton at time \(t\) hours can be expressed as \(D=10\sqrt{91t^2+80t+25}\) kilometres.

questions.stem: A body of still water has suffered an oil spill and a circular oil slick is floating on the surface of the water. The area of the oil slick is increasing by \(0.1\ \text{m}^{2}\text{ min}^{-1}\). At what rate is the radius increasing when the radius is \(0.3\ \text{m}\)?
questions.hint: Related rates: \(\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{dr}{dA}\times\dfrac{dA}{dt}\) with \(A=\pi r^{2}\).

steps.explain: Write what is given and what is asked.
The area of a circle is \(A=\pi r^{2}\). Differentiate with respect to \(r\).
Chain rule: \(\dfrac{dr}{dt}=\dfrac{dr}{dA}\times\dfrac{dA}{dt}\) and \(\dfrac{dr}{dA}=\dfrac{1}{2\pi r}\).
Substitute \(r=0.3\).
Common slip: using \(0.1\times 2\pi r\) instead of dividing gives \(0.1885\); options A, B and C come from arithmetic slips of this kind.
So the correct choice is option D.

keyPoints.text: At what rate is the radius increasing
keyPoints.note: Link the rates with the chain rule: dr/dt equals dr/dA times dA/dt.

Option B keeps the old limits, C forgets the \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) (36 instead of 12), D mis-evaluates \(u(5)\) as 6.

questions.stem: The graph of \(y=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{9+x^{2}}}\) for \(x>0\) is shown. The area bounded by \(y=\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{9+x^{2}}}\), the \(x\)-axis and the lines \(x=0\) and \(x=h\) is rotated about the \(x\)-axis to create a solid of revolution. Show that the volume of the solid is given by \(V=3\pi\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{h}{3}\right)\) cubic units. Which working is correct?
questions.hint: Volume of revolution about the \(x\)-axis: \(V=\pi\int y^{2}dx\) (SQUARE the \(y\)-value). Then \(\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}+x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\) with \(a=3\).

steps.explain: Each slice is a disc of radius \(y\) and thickness \(dx\), with volume \(\pi y^{2}dx\). Add them from \(x=0\) to \(x=h\) (shaded region rotated).
Square the function: the square root disappears.
Standard integral \(\int\dfrac{dx}{a^{2}+x^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{a}\) with \(a=3\): the factor is \(\dfrac{1}{3}\).
Substitute the limits; \(\tan^{-1}0=0\).
Why not the others: B uses \(\pi\int y\,dx\) (forgets to square); C forgets the \(\dfrac{1}{3}\) (giving \(9\pi\)); D integrates \(\dfrac{1}{9+x^{2}}\) as a log.
So the correct choice is option A.

questions.stem: The shaded region is enclosed by the curve \(y=3\sin\dfrac{x}{2}\), \(0\le x\le2\pi\), and the \(x\)-axis. This region is rotated through \(2\pi\) radians about the \(x\)-axis. Find the volume of the solid generated.
questions.hint: Volume of revolution about the \(x\)-axis: \(V=\pi\displaystyle\int y^{2}\,dx\). Square the function, then use \(\sin^{2}\theta=\dfrac{1}{2}(1-\cos2\theta)\) to integrate. Here \(\theta=\dfrac{x}{2}\), so \(2\theta=x\).

steps.explain: Formula: each thin strip becomes a disc of radius \(y\), so volume \(=\pi y^{2}dx\).
Use \(\sin^{2}A=\dfrac{1}{2}(1-\cos2A)\) with \(A=\dfrac{x}{2}\).
Integrate: \(\displaystyle\int(1-\cos x)dx=x-\sin x\).
Substitute the limits: \(\sin2\pi=0\) and \(\sin0=0\).
Why not the others: \(18\pi^{2}\) forgets the \(\dfrac{1}{2}\); \(9\pi\) misses the factor from the integral; \(12\pi\) is not obtained.

questions.stem: The graphs of the curves \(y=x^{2}\) and \(y=12-2x^{2}\) are shown in the diagram. The shaded region between the curves and the \(y\)-axis is rotated about the \(y\)-axis. By splitting the shaded region into two regions, or otherwise, find the volume of the solid formed.
questions.hint: Rotation about the \(y\)-axis: \(V=\pi\displaystyle\int x^{2}\,dy\). The boundary changes at \(y=4\) (where the curves meet): for \(0\le y\le4\) the right boundary is \(y=x^{2}\); for \(4\le y\le12\) it is \(y=12-2x^{2}\). Write \(x^{2}\) in terms of \(y\) for each.

steps.explain: Split at \(y=4\). For \(0\le y\le4\) the outer boundary is the curve \(y=x^{2}\), so \(x^{2}=y\).
For \(4\le y\le12\) the outer boundary is \(y=12-2x^{2}\): solve for \(x^{2}\): \(2x^{2}=12-y\), so \(x^{2}=6-\dfrac{y}{2}\).
Integrate \(V_{1}\).
Integrate \(V_{2}\): \(\displaystyle\int\left(6-\dfrac{y}{2}\right)dy=6y-\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}\).
Add the two volumes.
Why not the others: \(8\pi\) and \(16\pi\) are only one of the two parts; \(48\pi\) doubles the volume (the region is only the right half and is rotated once).
So the correct choice is option A.
